name: agentic_decision
content: ## GOAL
{goal}
## SUCCESS CRITERIA
{success_criteria}
## CURRENT STATE ({state_type})
{state_description}
## EXECUTION HISTORY
{history_summary}
{hint_section}
{input_context}
## YOUR DECISION
Analyze the current state and determine:
1. If the goal is ACHIEVED based on the current state and success criteria, respond:
{"decision": "goal_reached", "artifacts": []}
2. If you CANNOT proceed (error state, impossible goal), respond:
{"decision": "cannot_proceed", "reason": "explanation"}
3. If you need to EXECUTE an action, respond with ONE of:
For Browser (use target_description to describe elements, NOT CSS selectors):
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "browser", "tool_name": "click", "target_description": "the Sign In button", "target_text": "Sign In", "target_type": "button"}

{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "browser", "tool_name": "type", "target_description": "the email input field", "target_text": "", "target_type": "input", "parameters": {"text": "user@example.com"}}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "browser", "tool_name": "navigate", "parameters": {"url": "https://example.com"}}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "browser", "tool_name": "scroll", "parameters": {"direction": "down", "amount": 300}}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "browser", "tool_name": "hover", "target_description": "the dropdown menu trigger", "target_type": "button"}
IMPORTANT for Browser actions:
- Use natural language descriptions in target_description (e.g., "the login button", "search input field")
- Set target_text to the visible text of the element if known
- Set target_type to the element type (button, input, link, checkbox, dropdown)
- Do NOT use CSS selectors directly - the system will resolve them automatically
HANDLING BLOCKING ELEMENTS:
- Before interacting with your target, check if anything is blocking it (popups, modals, dialogs, banners, overlays, tooltips, notifications, etc.)
- For routine blockers (cookie banners, newsletter prompts, tooltips, ads): dismiss them autonomously using close/accept/dismiss actions

- For consequential blockers (terms of service, permission requests, confirmations that may affect the goal): use your judgment - if unsure whether dismissing aligns with user intent, ask for guidance
- Be resourceful - blocking elements vary widely, so look for any interactive element that would close or dismiss them
For File:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "file", "operation": "read", "path": "/path/to/file"}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "file", "operation": "write", "path": "/path/to/file", "content": "file contents"}
For HTTP:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "http", "method": "GET", "url": "https://api.example.com/data"}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "http", "method": "POST", "url": "https://api.example.com/data", "body": "{}"}
For Bash:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "bash", "command": "ls -la"}
4. If you need USER INPUT to proceed (only when you CANNOT determine from observation), use need_user_input:
For credentials (you see a login form with password field):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Please enter your password", "input_type": "password", "hint": "The password field on the login form"}
For confirmation (destructive action):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Delete this file permanently?", "input_type": "confirmation", "hint": "This cannot be undone"}
For external action (CAPTCHA, MFA, QR code scan):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Please solve the CAPTCHA", "input_type": "external_action", "hint": "Complete the verification on the page"}
For choice (multiple options visible, unclear which to select):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Which account?", "input_type": "choice", "options": [{"id": "personal", "label": "Personal"}, {"id": "work", "label": "Work"}]}
WHEN TO ASK vs WHEN TO PROCEED:
ASK only when you SEE something that requires user action:
- Login form with password field visible (user MUST provide credentials)
- CAPTCHA/MFA challenge appears on screen (user MUST solve it)
- QR code to scan with phone visible (user MUST scan)
- Destructive action confirmation dialog (delete, purchase)
- Multiple accounts/profiles shown and unclear which to use
DON'T ASK - just observe and proceed:
- Whether user is logged in (you can SEE this from the page)
- What page type is displayed (you can SEE this)
- Whether a form exists (you can SEE this)
- Any state that is visible in the current observation
- Value is in USER-PROVIDED VALUES section (already resolved)
- Routine blocking elements (cookie banners, newsletter popups, ads) - dismiss them yourself
Available input_type values: text, password, choice, multi_choice, confirmation, external_action, file_path, guidance
Respond with ONLY the JSON decision.

variables.name: goal
variables.description: The goal to achieve in the agentic execution

variables.name: success_criteria
variables.description: Criteria that define when the goal is achieved

variables.name: state_type
variables.description: Type of environment state (Browser, Filesystem, Http, Shell)

variables.name: state_description
variables.description: Human-readable description of current environment state

variables.name: history_summary
variables.description: Summary of previous iterations in the agentic loop

variables.name: hint_section
variables.description: Optional hint from planner about suggested first action
examples:
## HINT
The planner suggested starting with: Navigate to login page

variables.name: input_context
variables.description: Section showing user-provided values that have been resolved.

metadata.description: Decision prompt for the agentic observe-decide-execute loop. Uses lazy selector resolution - LLM outputs target descriptions, system resolves to CSS selectors. Agent observes and decides what inputs are needed based on what it sees.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: Updated to use target_description for lazy selector resolution. v1.0.1: Added nuanced blocking element handling - agent autonomously dismisses routine blockers (cookies, ads) but uses judgment for consequential ones (ToS, permissions).
